patient.name: Simone Campbell
patient.complaint: Dry cough, breathlessness and tiredness for 3 months, now a painful red eye
background: Black Caribbean heritage; lives in Lewisham
Never smoked; works as a pharmacist
No regular medicines, no known drug allergies

diagnosis.exam: Expect 'Which is the most likely diagnosis?' with a young Afro-Caribbean adult, dry cough, bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy and an extra-pulmonary clue (erythema nodosum, uveitis, lupus pernio, parotid swelling, facial palsy, hypercalcaemia). Löfgren's syndrome is the classic acute form.

points: Dry cough and breathless on stairs for 3 months.
Since Monday: **painful red left eye**, light hurts.

steps.lead: Simone has both risk factors: **Afro-Caribbean** heritage and a **family history**, at the typical age of 20 to 40.
A dry cough plus an inflamed eye in Simone suggests one **multisystem** granulomatous disease rather than two separate problems.

points: Left eye: red around the iris, small irregular pupil.
Tender red nodules on both shins.
No joint swelling, no parotid swelling.

steps.lead: Simone has the lung features plus **uveitis** and **erythema nodosum**. Lupus pernio, parotid swelling or facial palsy would be other clues.

steps.q: Which eye problem is typical of Simone's likely diagnosis?
steps.r: **Anterior uveitis** (painful red eye, photophobia, small pupil) is the classic sarcoid eye finding.

steps.lead: Simone's eye is the **anterior uveitis**; her bloods will be checked for raised **ACE** and **calcium**.

steps.title: Bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy: what else?
head: Feature
Sarcoidosis
TB
Lymphoma
rows: EN, uveitis, high ACE, high Ca

steps.lead: Simone does not have fever and arthralgia, so not **Löfgren's**. Fever + BHL + erythema nodosum + polyarthralgia would be.

steps.text: **Lupus pernio** is a purple rash on the nose and cheeks in sarcoidosis, despite its name. It is not SLE.
Bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy is sarcoid until proven otherwise; **unilateral** hilar enlargement should make you think of malignancy or TB.

investigation.exam: Expect 'most appropriate initial investigation' (chest X-ray: BHL), 'diagnostic investigation' (bronchoscopy with transbronchial biopsy: non-caseating granulomas), typical bloods (raised ACE, calcium, ESR) and Scadding staging.

steps.q: What is the first investigation for Simone's suspected sarcoidosis?
steps.r: The **chest X-ray** comes first: it shows bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy and stages the disease.

visual.title: Simone's chest X-ray
visual.caption: Bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy with mid-zone reticulonodular infiltrates.

steps.title: Simone's bloods
steps.text: High ACE, high calcium with a **suppressed PTH**: granuloma-driven, not parathyroid.

steps.lead: Simone's first tests fit: **BHL with infiltrates** on X-ray, raised **ACE**, **calcium** and **ESR**.

visual.title: Scadding stage on chest X-ray
visual.label: Simone stage 2
visual.caption: BHL plus interstitial infiltrates is stage 2.

steps.lead: Simone is **Scadding stage 2**: BHL plus infiltrates. Her pulmonary function tests show a **restrictive** pattern, used to monitor her.
Simone's stage comes straight from the **Scadding system**: 0 normal, 1 BHL, 2 BHL + infiltrates, 3 infiltrates only, 4 fibrosis.
Simone has **bronchoscopy with transbronchial biopsy**, which shows **non-caseating granulomas** and confirms the diagnosis.

steps.text: A raised ACE supports sarcoidosis but does not confirm it. **Biopsy** with non-caseating granulomas is the definitive test.

management.exam: Expect 'most appropriate management': reassurance and monitoring for mild stage 1/2 disease; oral prednisolone for symptomatic stage 2/3, hypercalcaemia, uveitis, neurological or cardiac disease; azathioprine if steroids fail or are contraindicated.

steps.q: Simone is stage 2, symptomatic, with uveitis and hypercalcaemia. What is first-line treatment?
steps.r: Symptomatic stage 2 disease, uveitis and hypercalcaemia are all indications for **oral prednisolone**.

steps.lead: Simone has three steroid indications: **parenchymal disease**, **uveitis** and **hypercalcaemia**, so she starts **oral prednisolone**.

steps.title: Who needs treatment?
nodes: Stage 1/2, mild, no organ threat → reassure and monitor
Symptomatic stage 2/3, hypercalcaemia, eye, nerve or heart → oral prednisolone
Steroids fail or contraindicated → oral azathioprine

visual.title: Simone on prednisolone
visual.caption: Calcium normalises and lung function improves as granuloma activity is suppressed.

steps.lead: If Simone's disease relapsed as steroids were reduced, or she could not take them, **oral azathioprine** would be next.
Simone has no palpitations or heart block. If she did, the notes give **methotrexate** for cardiac disease, and combination therapy for refractory disease.
Simone is followed in clinic with **lung function** and symptoms, watching for fibrosis, hypercalcaemia, heart and nerve involvement.
Simone is told that **severe breathlessness** would mean advanced lung involvement and needs **urgent assessment**.

steps.text: Asymptomatic stage 1 BHL found by chance often **resolves on its own**: reassure and monitor, no steroids.
Do not give oral steroids to everyone with sarcoid. Treat for **symptoms or organ threat** (lung, eye, calcium, nerve, heart).

science.exam: Expect applied questions: the biopsy description (non-caseating granulomas), why calcium rises (ectopic 1-alpha-hydroxylase), why hilar nodes are bilateral, why Löfgren's does well, and how it progresses to fibrosis.

steps.lead: Simone's biopsy shows tight clusters of **epithelioid macrophages** and **giant cells** with lymphocytes around them, and **no necrosis**.

steps.q: Why is Simone's PTH low while her calcium is high?
steps.r: Granuloma macrophages express **1-alpha-hydroxylase**, making calcitriol outside renal control; high calcium then suppresses PTH.

steps.title: Why Simone's calcium is high
nodes: More calcium absorbed from the gut

steps.lead: Simone's raised **ACE** reflects her granuloma burden, and her high calcium comes from granuloma-made **active vitamin D**.
Simone's hilar nodes are **bilateral** because granulomas infiltrate the mediastinal and hilar nodes on both sides.
If Simone had **Löfgren's**, her outlook would be better: it is acute and usually resolves on its own.
Simone is treated partly to stop progression to **stage 4 fibrosis**; steroids damp down T cells and macrophages.

glossary.Sarcoidosis: Multisystem disease of non-caseating granulomas, mainly in the lungs and lymph nodes.
glossary.Granuloma: A compact cluster of activated macrophages and other immune cells walling off an antigen.
glossary.Non-caseating: Without central cheese-like necrosis; typical of sarcoid granulomas.
glossary.Caseating: With central cheesy necrosis; typical of TB granulomas.
glossary.Epithelioid cells: Activated macrophages that look like epithelial cells, forming granulomas.
glossary.Giant cells: Large cells with many nuclei, formed by fused macrophages in granulomas.
glossary.BHL: Bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy: enlarged lymph nodes at both lung roots.
glossary.Bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy: Enlarged lymph nodes at both lung roots; the classic X-ray sign of sarcoidosis.
glossary.Hilar: Relating to the lung root, where the bronchi, vessels and lymph nodes enter.
glossary.Löfgren's syndrome: Acute sarcoidosis with fever, BHL, erythema nodosum and polyarthralgia; good prognosis.
glossary.Erythema nodosum: Painful, red, raised nodules, usually on the shins.
glossary.Lupus pernio: Purple, indurated rash on the nose and cheeks in sarcoidosis; not related to SLE.
glossary.Uveitis: Inflammation of the uvea; anterior uveitis causes a painful red eye and photophobia.
glossary.Anterior uveitis: Inflammation of the iris and ciliary body: painful red eye, photophobia, small pupil.
glossary.Parotid: The large salivary gland in front of the ear.
glossary.LMN: Lower motor neurone; an LMN facial palsy weakens the whole half of the face, forehead included.
glossary.ACE: Angiotensin-converting enzyme; made by granulomas, so raised in active sarcoidosis.
glossary.Hypercalcaemia: Raised blood calcium; causes thirst, polyuria, constipation and confusion.
glossary.PTH: Parathyroid hormone; suppressed when calcium is raised by a non-parathyroid cause.
glossary.PTHrP: Parathyroid hormone-related protein, made by some cancers to raise calcium.
glossary.1-alpha-hydroxylase: Enzyme that converts vitamin D to its active form, calcitriol.
glossary.Calcitriol: 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D, the active form that increases gut calcium absorption.
glossary.ESR: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate; a non-specific marker of inflammation.
glossary.Scadding: Chest X-ray staging of sarcoidosis from 0 (normal) to 4 (fibrosis).
glossary.Transbronchial biopsy: Lung tissue sample taken through a bronchoscope.
glossary.Bronchoscopy: Looking inside the airways with a flexible camera.
glossary.Restrictive pattern: Spirometry with FEV1/FVC above 0.7 but low FEV1 and FVC.
glossary.TLCO: Transfer factor for carbon monoxide: how well gas crosses into the blood.
glossary.Prednisolone: Oral corticosteroid; first-line for symptomatic or organ-threatening sarcoidosis.
glossary.Azathioprine: Immunosuppressant used when steroids fail or are contraindicated.
glossary.Methotrexate: Antifolate immunosuppressant used as a steroid-sparing agent.
glossary.Cardiac sarcoidosis: Granulomas in the heart causing heart block, arrhythmias or heart failure.
glossary.Reed-Sternberg cells: Large abnormal B cells that define Hodgkin lymphoma.
glossary.Heerfordt syndrome: Sarcoid with uveitis, parotid swelling, fever and facial nerve palsy.

technique.stem: A 29 year old Black Caribbean man has a 2 month history of dry cough, breathlessness on exertion and tiredness. Last week he developed a painful red right eye with blurred vision and photophobia. His chest is clear on auscultation. His chest X-ray shows bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy.
technique.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

steps.x: A diagnosis question: BHL in a young adult, plus a second-system clue.
Young, Afro-Caribbean, dry cough, anterior uveitis, BHL.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: Lung cancer is in older smokers, usually with a unilateral hilum.
Hodgkin gives night sweats, itch and asymmetrical nodes, not uveitis.
SLE gives rash, joint and kidney disease, not BHL.
TB gives fevers, sweats, weight loss and usually unilateral nodes.

steps.x: **C. Sarcoidosis.** Rule: young Afro-Caribbean + BHL + uveitis = sarcoid.

technique.stem: A 34 year old woman has a 3 month history of dry cough and breathlessness. She has tender red nodules on both shins. Her temperature is 37.3°C, pulse rate 84 bpm, BP 116/72 mmHg, respiratory rate 18 breaths per minute and oxygen saturation 97% breathing air. Her GP suspects sarcoidosis.
technique.q: Which is the most appropriate initial investigation?

clues: tender red nodules on both shins
steps.x: Erythema nodosum and chest symptoms: suspected sarcoid.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Chest X-ray**: BHL, infiltrates, and Scadding stage.

elim: Biopsy is definitive but not the first test.
HRCT comes after the chest X-ray.
ACE supports but cannot confirm and is not the first test.
Spirometry monitors; it does not show BHL.

steps.x: **B. Chest X-ray.** Rule: initial = CXR; definitive = biopsy.

technique.stem: A 46 year old woman has stage 2 pulmonary sarcoidosis treated with oral prednisolone for 9 months. Each time the dose is reduced below 10 mg, her cough and breathlessness return. She has developed steroid-induced diabetes and a vertebral fragility fracture. Her FVC has fallen from 82% to 70% of predicted.
technique.q: Which is the most appropriate next step in management?

steps.x: Next step when first-line treatment is failing.

clues: Each time the dose is reduced
steps.x: Steroid-dependent, steroid side effects, progressing disease.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: More steroid worsens her diabetes and bones.
Inhaled steroids do not control parenchymal sarcoid.
Her disease is progressing.
Stopping would let it progress to fibrosis.

steps.x: **C. Oral azathioprine.** Rule: steroids fail or contraindicated = azathioprine.

technique.stem: A 31 year old woman has bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, a dry cough and erythema nodosum. She has a bronchoscopy with transbronchial biopsy. Stains and cultures for acid-fast bacilli are negative and there are no atypical lymphocytes.
technique.q: Which is the most likely histological finding?

steps.x: A histology question: make the diagnosis, then its tissue finding.
Sarcoid; TB and lymphoma made unlikely.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: Caseating granulomas are TB; AFB negative.
Reed-Sternberg cells are Hodgkin lymphoma.
Small round blue cells suggest small cell carcinoma or lymphoma.
Squamous nests are squamous cell carcinoma.

practice.stem: A 38 year old Black woman has had purple, raised, firm plaques on her nose and cheeks for 6 months. She also has a dry cough and breathlessness on hills. She has no joint pain, mouth ulcers or photosensitivity. Her chest X-ray shows bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy with reticulonodular shadowing.
practice.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
practice.e: Purple plaques on the nose and cheeks are lupus pernio, a sarcoid skin lesion; with BHL this is sarcoidosis. Despite the name, lupus pernio is not SLE.

clues: purple, raised, firm plaques on her nose and cheeks
no joint pain, mouth ulcers or photosensitivity
steps.x: Lupus pernio + BHL; SLE features absent.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: Discoid lupus causes scarring plaques, not BHL.
Rosacea is flushing and pustules, not purple plaques with lung disease.
SLE has joint pain, ulcers, photosensitivity; none here.
No fevers, sweats or weight loss; BHL is bilateral.

steps.x: **C. Sarcoidosis.** Rule: lupus pernio = sarcoid, not lupus.

practice.stem: A 27 year old woman has a 1 week history of fever, painful swollen ankles and tender red lumps on both shins. Her temperature is 38.0°C, pulse rate 96 bpm, BP 118/70 mmHg, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute and oxygen saturation 98% breathing air. Her chest X-ray shows bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy.
practice.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
practice.e: Fever, bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, erythema nodosum and polyarthralgia is Löfgren's syndrome, the acute form of sarcoidosis with a good prognosis.

clues: tender red lumps on both shins
steps.x: Fever + polyarthralgia + erythema nodosum + BHL: all four.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: Behçet's has oral and genital ulcers, not BHL.
Reactive arthritis follows GI or GU infection, with conjunctivitis and urethritis.
Rheumatic fever follows strep throat, with carditis.
TB rarely gives bilateral BHL with an acute arthropathy.

practice.stem: A 40 year old man has 2 months of thirst, passing more urine, constipation and a dry cough. His temperature is 36.9°C, pulse rate 80 bpm, BP 128/82 mmHg, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute and oxygen saturation 96% breathing air. His chest X-ray shows bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy.
practice.q: Which is the most likely cause of his hypercalcaemia?
practice.e: Hypercalcaemia with a suppressed PTH, raised ACE and bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy in a 40 year old is sarcoidosis. Primary hyperparathyroidism would have a raised or inappropriately normal PTH.

steps.x: Cause of hypercalcaemia: check the PTH first.
Labs: calcium high, PTH suppressed, ACE high. Symptomatic hypercalcaemia with BHL.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: Prostate metastases are in older men, usually sclerotic.
Myeloma: older, renal failure, bone pain, no BHL.
PTH would be high or normal, not suppressed.
Squamous carcinoma (PTHrP) is in older smokers with a hilar mass.

practice.stem: A 32 year old woman with sarcoidosis has a 3 day history of a painful red left eye, blurred vision and pain when she looks at bright light. Her temperature is 36.8°C, pulse rate 78 bpm, BP 120/76 mmHg, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute and oxygen saturation 98% breathing air. The redness is most marked around the iris and the left pupil is small.
practice.q: Which is the most likely finding on slit-lamp examination?
practice.e: A painful red eye with photophobia, circumcorneal redness and a small pupil in sarcoidosis is anterior uveitis, its classic eye complication.

steps.x: A finding question: the eye feature of sarcoid.

clues: pain when she looks at bright light

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: CRAO is sudden painless loss of vision.
A dendritic ulcer is herpes simplex keratitis.
Dry eye is gritty, not photophobic with a small pupil.
Papilloedema is painless disc swelling.

practice.stem: A 30 year old woman has weakness of the left side of her face, including her forehead, that developed over 2 days. She has also noticed painless swelling in front of both ears, a dry mouth and a dry cough for 2 months. Her temperature is 37.4°C, pulse rate 82 bpm and BP 116/74 mmHg. Chest X-ray (see item resources).
practice.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
practice.e: LMN facial palsy, bilateral parotid swelling, a dry cough and bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy is sarcoidosis. Bell's palsy would not explain the parotids or BHL.

steps.x: Diagnosis: link the face, parotids and chest.

clues: swelling in front of both ears
steps.x: LMN facial palsy + bilateral parotid swelling + cough; CXR shows BHL.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: Bell's palsy is isolated; it does not explain parotids or BHL.
Lymphoma rarely gives a facial palsy with symmetrical parotids.
Mumps is acute, painful, febrile, without BHL.
Sjögren's gives dry eyes and mouth but not BHL or facial palsy.

practice.stem: A 36 year old man has stage 2 pulmonary sarcoidosis confirmed on transbronchial biopsy. He has a dry cough and breathlessness on exertion. His chest X-ray shows bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy with reticulonodular infiltrates. He has pulmonary function tests.
practice.q: Which is the most likely result of his pulmonary function tests?
o: Obstruction with large reversibility after salbutamol
Restriction with FEV1/FVC above 0.7 and reduced TLCO
practice.e: Parenchymal sarcoidosis gives a restrictive pattern (ratio above 0.7, low volumes) with a reduced TLCO; PFTs are used to monitor it.

steps.x: A finding question: which lung function pattern.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: Symptomatic infiltrates are unlikely to give normal tests.
A low ratio is obstruction (COPD).
Large reversibility is asthma.
TLCO is reduced, not raised, in interstitial disease.

practice.stem: A 35 year old woman has a dry cough, erythema nodosum and bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy on chest X-ray. Her temperature is 37.1°C, pulse rate 80 bpm, BP 118/76 mmHg, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute and oxygen saturation 97% breathing air.
practice.q: Which is the most appropriate investigation to confirm the diagnosis?
practice.e: Bronchoscopy with transbronchial biopsy showing non-caseating granulomas is definitive. A raised ACE and calcium support but do not confirm sarcoidosis.

steps.x: Labs: raised ACE, calcium, ESR. Sarcoid is likely; tissue confirms it.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: HRCT characterises but does not give tissue.
Repeating calcium adds nothing.
Vitamin D does not make the diagnosis.
A tuberculin test may help exclude TB but cannot confirm sarcoid.

practice.stem: A 44 year old man has had sarcoidosis for 6 years. He has increasing breathlessness. His new chest X-ray shows reticulonodular interstitial infiltrates in both lungs. The bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy seen on previous films has resolved, and there is no honeycombing or volume loss.
practice.q: Which is the most likely Scadding stage?
practice.e: Interstitial infiltrates without bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy is Scadding stage 3. Stage 2 has both; stage 4 is fibrosis.

clues: hilar lymphadenopathy seen on previous films has resolved
steps.x: Infiltrates yes, BHL no, fibrosis no.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: Stage 0 is a normal film.
Stage 1 is BHL alone.
Stage 2 is BHL plus infiltrates; the BHL has gone.
Stage 4 is fibrosis; none here.

practice.stem: A 29 year old man has bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy found on a chest X-ray for a work medical. He has no symptoms. Examination is normal. Transbronchial biopsy shows non-caseating granulomas. His calcium, eye examination, ECG and lung function are all normal.
practice.q: Which is the most appropriate management?
practice.e: Asymptomatic stage 1 sarcoidosis with no organ involvement often resolves spontaneously, so reassurance and monitoring is appropriate. Steroids are for symptoms or organ threat.

clues: calcium, eye examination, ECG and lung function are all normal

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: Not a treatment for sarcoid lung disease.
Methotrexate is for cardiac or refractory disease.
Azathioprine is second-line after steroids.
No indication for steroids.

practice.stem: A 37 year old woman has sarcoidosis with worsening breathlessness. Chest X-ray shows bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy with interstitial infiltrates. Her temperature is 36.9°C, pulse rate 90 bpm, BP 122/78 mmHg, respiratory rate 20 breaths per minute and oxygen saturation 94% breathing air.
practice.q: Which is the most appropriate initial management?
practice.e: Symptomatic stage 2 disease with hypercalcaemia needs first-line oral corticosteroids. Azathioprine is second-line; reassurance is only for mild disease.

steps.x: Stage 2, symptomatic; labs: calcium 2.95, low FVC, rising creatinine.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: Inhaled steroids do not treat parenchymal sarcoid or calcium.
Azathioprine is second-line.
Methotrexate is for cardiac or refractory disease.
She has organ threat now.

steps.x: **D. Oral prednisolone.** Rule: symptomatic or hypercalcaemia = steroids.

practice.stem: A 41 year old man with stage 2 pulmonary sarcoidosis has responded to oral prednisolone, which is now being slowly reduced. He feels well. His calcium has returned to normal. He asks how his sarcoidosis will be followed up.
practice.q: Which is the most appropriate way to monitor his disease?
o: Pulmonary function tests and symptom review
practice.e: Sarcoidosis is monitored with lung function tests and symptoms, watching for relapse and fibrosis. ACE alone is not reliable; repeat biopsies are not needed.

clues: how his sarcoidosis will be followed up
steps.x: Risk of relapse as steroids taper; risk of fibrosis.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: Relapse on tapering is common.
Biopsy is diagnostic, not for routine monitoring.
Monthly PET-CT is excessive radiation.
ACE alone does not track lung function.

practice.stem: A 35 year old woman with sarcoidosis has thirst, polyuria and constipation. She takes no supplements. Her PTH is suppressed and her 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D level is raised despite a normal 25-hydroxyvitamin D level.
practice.q: Which is the most likely mechanism of her hypercalcaemia?
o: Reduced renal calcium excretion from thiazides
practice.e: Granuloma macrophages express 1-alpha-hydroxylase, converting vitamin D to calcitriol outside renal control; gut calcium absorption rises and PTH is suppressed.

steps.x: Excess conversion to active vitamin D, PTH-independent.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: PTH is suppressed.
No bone lesions; calcitriol is high.
PTHrP would not raise calcitriol.
She takes no thiazides.
